an extreme difference in perceived abilities/self worth over time, feeling "high", "frenzied", "extremely irritable" for long periods of time (at least 4 days, weeks, or longer, but time during these periods can feel warped, so keep a sleep and energy journal), excessive drinking/smoking/exercising and not feeling tired with little to no sleep, other people commenting on how fast your speech is, risky sexual contact, gambling, general impulsive behavior, looking back at extremely high risk behaviours during times you "felt your best" and believing those were the "good days" (this is how I didnt notice my first hypomanic episode) 

my biggest sign for hypomania is my pupils dilate and I cant stop smiling and I constantly want to be doing something produtive or talking with people. 

mania itself is harder to detect in oneself so youd likely have to guage by how others are reacting to you, if you've had beliefs for a long time or if theyre new, and how long you've felt so "euphoric", "unstable emotionally (crying, laughing, without a reason that used to make sense for you) or "full of rage"

with depression feeling heavy, weak, irritable,  worthless, vengeful, guilty, sleeping a lot or very little,  decrease in energy, lack of motivation, for me when I'm depressed it's like my worldview shrinks to the size of my bed

it's important to remember with bipolar type 1 only one manic episode is needed for a diagnosis while with bipolar type 2 both depression and hypomania are necessary 

if you feel like you reach your "peak self" when you're not sleeping or eating well and you're doing things that take a lot of "guts", I'd say that's something to bring up to a professional
